assets.CREDITS.md:
# Credits

All five images in this folder are placeholder art generated for this
example campaign — a flat colour, a border, and the scene's own name and
one-line description, produced with Pillow. No illustration, no external
source, nothing to attribute.

Swap any of them for real art at any time: the scene files reference them by
path (`assets/<name>.jpg`), so replacing the file is enough — no JSON needs
to change unless the filename does too.

tree.README.md:
# campaigns/example — demo content

A small, self-contained campaign that ships with the repo (unlike every other
folder under `campaigns/`, which `.gitignore` treats as personal session data
and keeps out of git). Its only job is to show the file shapes `dm/importing.md`
describes, filled in with something a stranger can open and immediately
understand — one case, five scenes, five NPCs, one pre-made player.

Pick this folder in **Buscar campaña** / **Cargar campaña** to see a working
table: a scene with a roster, a grid scene with multiple monsters on it, a
quest-giver NPC, and a fully-built character export.

The art in `assets/` is generated placeholder, not real illustration — see
`assets/CREDITS.md`. Everything else (scenes, monsters, the character, the
story notes) is real content, just for a campaign that does not exist outside
this folder.

runs.README.md:
# runs/

Una carpeta por mesa. Cada una tiene su propia gente (`players/`), su propia
partida (`session.json`) y sus propias notas — y puede tener su versión de un
monstruo, un objeto o una escena, que tapa la de la campaña mientras juega.

La campaña de arriba la comparten todas.

story.00-the-vanishing.md:
# The Vanishing

Curdmoor's Grand Wheel has sat under its ceremonial dome in Cheese Square for
eleven generations, ever since a travelling god named Cheddrick — evicted
from his last temple over unpaid rent, and unwilling to go through that again
— blessed a passing dairy cart instead and settled for being worshipped in
wheel form. Nobody has ever properly explained why the town went along with
this. It has simply always been true, the way Tuesdays are true.

The night before the Cheese Festival, the dome is found standing open and the
Wheel is gone. No forced locks, no ransom note, no sign of a struggle — just
a stone pedestal with a wheel-shaped dent in it, some rind crumbs, and one
claw mark far too large for anything that should have fit through the door.

Mayor Bartleby Crumbwell, up for re-election the week after the festival,
hires the party in Cheese Square before the brass band has even finished
tuning up. His terms are simple: find the Wheel before dawn, or explain to
eleven generations of tradition — and several thousand furious voters — why
it isn't there.
story.01-the-suspects.md:
# The Suspects

Two leads surface fast, and both are wrong in an interesting way.

**The Order of the Sacred Rind**, met at the Content Goat, believe the Wheel
is Cheddrick's literal earthly body and that eating it is scripture, not
theft. They are loud, self-righteous about it, and — this is the
disappointing part for anyone hoping for a straightforward cult bust —
completely innocent. They wanted to eat the Wheel in a big public ceremony,
not smuggle it into a sewer. A cultist who is offended at being suspected of
*subtlety* is a good tell that this lead is a dead end.

**Inspector Mildew Grey**, found already poking around the empty shrine, was
sent by the rival town of Brinemarsh with a forged writ and genuine
professional jealousy, to sabotage the festival somehow. He arrived to find
the job already done for him and has spent the day trying to look
responsible for it, clipboard held very seriously, seal made from a
bottlecap. He is guilty of fraud and nothing else.

Neither of them noticed the claw mark. Neither of them can explain the smell.
story.02-the-reveal.md:
# The Reveal

The claw mark leads down into the Curdy Sewers, past three unusually large
and unusually confident rats who have been living off drips from the Wheel
for weeks without ever finding the source. Following the smell past them
leads to a warm, round burrow, and the entire Grand Wheel of Curdmoor, being
used as a pillow by a giant mole roughly the size of a cart.

His name, once anyone thinks to ask, is Gerald. He tunnelled in because the
shrine smelled incredible, dragged the whole Wheel home the way anyone would
drag home a good pillow, and has had no idea since that an entire town has
been in an uproar about it. He is not a boss fight unless the party makes it
one — he will trade the Wheel for literally any other food, mildly confused
about why nobody offered earlier.

The Wheel goes back on its pedestal in time for the festival, missing one
Gerald-sized bite that the Mayor decides not to mention in his speech.
Gerald himself is adopted as the festival's mascot within the week, on the
theory that a monster the town caught is a much better story than a monster
the town is still afraid of. He attends the following year's festival in a
small ceremonial hat and falls asleep during the anthem.
story.README.md:
# Story notes

Working notes for this campaign's one case so far — the disappearance of the
Grand Wheel of Curdmoor, the night before the Cheese Festival.

- [[The Vanishing]] — the hook, and why the party gets hired
- [[The Suspects]] — the two red herrings the party will chase first
- [[The Reveal]] — where the trail actually leads, and how the case closes

Status: **closed**. Play it straight or play it broad — Gerald does not negotiate well
either way.
